study.setting: Single infant with neonatal-onset inherited CPS1 deficiency; uncontrolled expanded-access clinical case

endpoints.group_window_precision: Figure baseline: age three months until first intervention; between interventions; after second intervention. Exact specimen timestamps and group counts not supplied numerically in inspected clinical text.

groups.label: Age three months until first intervention

endpoints.group_window_precision: Baseline; steady state after first intervention; steady state after second intervention. Steady-state boundaries and specimen timestamps not specified numerically. These are not established as the same windows or paired specimens as ammonia.

weight.interpretation: A growing infant; no untreated growth comparator or attribution of growth to editing. Percentile change is not a percent increase in weight.

care_and_outcomes.medication_fraction_precision: Source describes approximately half of the starting nitrogen-scavenger requirement; no medication amounts or regimen reconstructed.
care_and_outcomes.initial_wean_reason_reversed: Rising glutamine led clinicians to restore the initial nitrogen-scavenger requirement.
care_and_outcomes.protein_context: Protein targets changed with care. Birth at 35 weeks gestation complicates comparison with chronological-age recommended allowance. Source reports increased tolerance and later full-protein feeding during illness; no raw protein-intake series extracted.
supportive_care: Sirolimus and tacrolimus immunosuppression around the intervention period
Intravenous fluids and one protein-free day during the first post-intervention respiratory illness
illness_context: Respiratory viral infection after the first intervention
Two viral illnesses with vomiting and diarrhea after the second intervention
other_events: Coughing episode during the second intervention resolved with nasal suctioning
Transient ALT and AST elevations after the second intervention and again with viral illness
care_and_outcomes.neurologic_status: Reported stable over the original short follow-up; no demonstrated reversal of prior injury or long-term developmental trajectory
